title: Bangers and Mash
subtitle: Pork sausages with creamy mash and onion gravy
excerpt: Homemade pork sausage shapes served on buttery mash with a rich onion gravy. A British comfort food classic that comes together on the hob in under an hour.
sourceNotes: Bangers and mash has been a British staple since at least the First World War, when sausages were nicknamed bangers because their high water content caused them to burst when cooked. The dish became firmly embedded in British pub culture through the mid 20th century.

content.text: Shape the pork mince into firm sausages before frying. Chilling them briefly helps them hold their shape in the pan.
Season the pork mince well with salt and pepper. Shape into 8 sausages and chill for 10 minutes while you prepare the other components.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 18 to 20 minutes until tender. Drain and return to the pan. Mash with the butter and warm milk until smooth. Season generously and keep warm with a lid on.
Fry the sausages in a lightly oiled pan over medium heat, turning regularly, for 12 to 15 minutes until cooked through and browned all over. Set aside to rest.
In the same pan, add a splash of oil and fry the sliced onions over medium-low heat for 15 minutes, stirring often, until soft and golden. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the beef stock and Worcestershire sauce. Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring, until the gravy thickens slightly. Season to taste. Serve the sausages on the mash with plenty of gravy spooned over.

items.symptom: Sausages fall apart in the pan
items.cause: Mince was not packed firmly enough
items.fix: Squeeze the mince tightly when shaping and chill before frying.

items.cause: Not enough flour or not simmered long enough
items.fix: Simmer for longer, or stir in a little more flour mixed with cold water.

items.cause: Potatoes were over-mashed or too watery
items.fix: Drain potatoes well and mash gently. Do not use a blender.
